text: Circadian rhythms regulate human epidermal stem cells: core clock genes peak in successive, phased waves across the 24 hr day, each wave linked to transcript subsets that temporally segregate responsiveness to proliferation/differentiation cues (TGFβ, calcium); circadian arrhythmia profoundly impairs stem cell function in vitro and in vivo, possibly contributing to aging and carcinogenesis. Using the FANTOM5 panel covering most human tissues and cell types, an atlas of active in vivo-transcribed enhancers was produced; enhancers resemble CpG-poor mRNA promoters, generating bidirectional, exosome-sensitive, short unspliced RNAs, enabling comparison of regulatory programs, identification of disease-associated regulatory SNPs, and classification of cell-type-specific versus ubiquitous enhancers. p38MAPK drives age-induced expression of multiple cell cycle inhibitors: dominant-negative p38(AF) mice (Thr180/Tyr182 mutated) show attenuated p38 signaling and inhibitor expression in organs including pancreatic islets, and aged p38(AF/+) mice display enhanced islet proliferation and regeneration versus wild-type littermates.
